review_candidates.title: Staff Software Engineer, Data Infrastructure
review_candidates.description: TL;DR: Build the data infrastructure the Lovable agent runs on: ingestion, storage and query for millions of small tenants instead of one large one. You'll join the Data Platform team, and your work decides whether the apps people build on Lovable can rely on their data. Why Lovable? Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started. We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software. What We’re Looking For An infrastructure engineer who has built and run data systems in production at scale, and wants the harder version of the problem: millions of tiny tenants on shared infrastructure. Deep experience in at least one layer (ingestion, storage formats and table layout, query execution, or orchestration), and the range to work across the others. Experience with multi-tenant or untrusted workloads: isolation, noisy neighbours, and keeping cost per tenant low. Good judgment on calls no one can check for you: the right abstraction, the tradeoff between cost and latency, whether a design holds at 10x. You work with AI agents end to end. Your output is the systems you build, not the code you type by hand. You ship, and you own what you ship in production. What You’ll Do Build ingestion that accepts events from millions of Lovable apps, treats every producer as untrusted, and keeps one tenant's bad traffic from slowing or corrupting another's data. Build managed analytical storage for every user, including schema management, partitioning, and compaction of a constant stream of small writes. Make queries fast when you can't keep compute warm for every tenant. Build the runtime for agent-written connectors: isolated execution, credentials, scheduling, retries and state. Make cost per tenant measurable, then drive it down, through metering, limits and workload isolation. Expose data, metadata and tools to the Lovable agent so it can build software on customers' data. Run what you build, including observability, freshness and recovery. The tech stack We're building with tools that both humans and AI love: Languages: Go, Rust, Python, SQL Data: ClickHouse, BigQuery, Parquet on object storage Streaming & orchestration: Pub/Sub, Temporal Cloud: GCP, Cloudflare, AWS DevOps & tooling: GitHub Actions, Grafana, OTEL, Terraform And always on the lookout for what's next. About Your Application Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join. We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

review_candidates.title: Senior Software Engineer
review_candidates.description: UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable. Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia. UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems. About The Role UFORCE is looking for a Senior Engineer to help build the software that makes uncrewed vehicle (UxV) operations more reliable, repeatable, and scalable. You’ll develop capabilities across the UFORCE C2/C4ISR stack, with a focus on automating operational workflows, improving mission readiness, and reducing the burden on operators and pilots. You’ll combine hands-on backend and frontend engineering with end-to-end product ownership: understanding operational needs, designing solutions, shipping capabilities, and validating them with real-world crews. You’ll work closely with operators, product teams, and engineers across systems, building software that remains usable in air-gapped environments, over intermittent connections, and with limited access to engineering support. What You’ll Do Build and improve pre-flight and post-flight workflows, including automated checks, configuration, mission package handling, log capture, and post-mission data synchronization. Develop operator-facing interfaces and guardrails that make routine workflows intuitive, consistent, and less dependent on engineering intervention. Standardize configuration and mission setup patterns to reduce manual work and variation between crews and platforms. Build operational analytics that help teams understand readiness, workflow performance, turnaround time, and the impact of connectivity constraints. Work directly with operators to identify friction, translate field feedback into requirements, and validate improvements in real operational workflows. Design and maintain APIs, schemas, and event models that enable reliable integrations and parallel development across teams. Own delivery from discovery and technical design through implementation, rollout, observability, and iteration. Make architectural trade-offs explicit, balancing product needs with compatibility, deployment constraints, and supportability in the field. Create concise runbooks, checklists, and troubleshooting guidance that help crews operate independently and reduce avoidable errors. Unblock teammates and partner teams through clear interfaces, ownership boundaries, and practical engineering standards. Required Skills 6+ years of backend or full-stack engineering experience delivering production systems. Strong hands-on experience with Node.js and React in production environments. A product-focused approach: you understand user needs and turn complex workflows into practical, usable software. Experience building and operating API-first services, including versioning, backward compatibility, and contract-driven development. Practical experience with Docker and Kubernetes, including deployments, debugging, and operational monitoring. Strong end-to-end engineering ownership, from discovery and technical design to rollout and continuous improvement. Ability to work closely with users, translate operational feedback into technical requirements, and validate whether a solution delivers the intended outcome. Clear written and verbal communication, particularly when explaining interfaces, constraints, and technical trade-offs across teams. A practical approach to debugging and reliability, supported by useful telemetry, clear documentation, and follow-through. What Success Looks Like Key pre-flight and post-flight workflows are automated, reducing manual steps and reliance on tribal knowledge. Mission readiness and turnaround time improve, with clear before-and-after measurements. Operators can complete routine configuration and mission setup independently, using consistent workflows and practical guardrails. Teams have reliable operational data and review workflows to identify bottlenecks and prioritize improvements. Shared APIs, schemas, and event models reduce integration friction and enable teams to develop in parallel. Delivered capabilities work in real field conditions and are supported by useful telemetry, concise runbooks, and clear ownership. The nature of combat has changed. Tomorrow’s battlefield success depends on autonomy, speed, and adaptability. And UFORCE is ready. Are You?
